subjective: Pixie, a young female Indian Pariah dog, has been showing signs of slight digestive upset for one to two weeks. The owner reports no loose stools but slightly loose toes. Pixie vomited a few days ago after eating chicken soup and rice, which was mashed and strained to avoid bones. She has been crying and uncomfortable, especially at night, and has not slept well since 4 am due to apparent abdominal pain. Appetite is generally good, with some reluctance to eat curd. The owner notes Pixie is fidgety and restless, sometimes rolling due to pain. Pixie has only received her first vaccination.
objective: Physical examination reveals slight protrusion of the intestine, possibly due to heavy worm burden. No bones were observed in vomitus. Pixie is active but vibrating and fidgety. No signs of severe dehydration or other systemic abnormalities noted. Owner reports no loose stools but slight looseness in toes. No mucous or blood noted in stool. Vomitus was of normal consistency without foreign material. No fever or other vital signs documented in the conversation.
assessment: Possible gastrointestinal obstruction or intussusception secondary to heavy worm burden or other causes. Abdominal pain is evident, causing restlessness and crying. Vomiting episode noted but without foreign bodies. Slight digestive upset possibly related to recent diet change. Need to rule out serious conditions such as intussusception or obstruction via imaging.
plan: Schedule abdominal X-ray at the 2 o'clock appointment to evaluate for obstruction or intussusception. Advise feeding liquids and normal food as tolerated, avoiding sudden diet changes. Monitor for worsening signs such as increased vomiting, lethargy, or severe abdominal pain. Use towel or basket for safe transport. Continue monitoring appetite and stool consistency. Follow up after imaging to determine further treatment. Maintain vaccination schedule and observe for any infectious disease precautions.
conclusion: Pixie is a young female Indian Pariah dog presenting with signs of mild gastrointestinal upset including vomiting, slight looseness of stools, and abdominal pain causing restlessness and crying. Physical examination suggests possible intestinal protrusion likely related to heavy worm burden, raising concern for intussusception or obstruction. An abdominal X-ray is planned to confirm diagnosis. Supportive care with cautious feeding and monitoring is advised. Owner instructed on safe transport and follow-up plans. Vaccination status noted as first dose only, with clinic precautions in place.
